context: Select the smallest web foundation that supports Sprint-1 local persistence and a Sprint-2 server seam without pre-empting the unresolved MCL-1 Minecraft-versus-standalone decision.
hard_constraints: HC-001 no Minecraft loader/engine selection before MCL-1

candidates.name: React/Vite SPA plus separate API later
candidates.summary: Static/browser-first client with a second backend project introduced for Sprint 2.
risks: Sprint 2 creates a second runtime/deployment surface before independent operations are demonstrated.
non_risks: Local IndexedDB works naturally in a SPA.
sensitivity_points: Whether the backend must become independently operated.
tradeoff_points: Static simplicity now versus two-runtime coordination later.

candidates.name: Next.js modular monolith with ports/adapters
candidates.summary: One web deployable, framework-free domain/application modules, IndexedDB now and route/server adapters later.
risks: Web and future server delivery share one deployable.
Framework adapter has not completed a clean install/build in this generation environment.
non_risks: A repository port isolates IndexedDB from the application layer.
Next.js provides a future server delivery seam without requiring another service.
tradeoff_points: One-deployable simplicity versus independent backend deployment.

candidates.name: Polyglot monorepo with Web, API, Supabase and Minecraft loader now
candidates.summary: Pre-build all imagined deployment and game-runtime surfaces.

hard_constraint_results.notes: Requires a loader/engine commitment while MCL-1 is open.

tradeoff_points: Speculative future coverage versus immediate complexity and irreversible commitment.

strongest_counterargument: If the web experience is confirmed as static/offline-first and the backend must be independently owned/deployed, a Vite SPA plus separate API is structurally cleaner and avoids coupling backend delivery to Next.js.
decision_rationale: Meets all currently observed web hard constraints.
Provides the Sprint-2 server seam without introducing a second service now.
Ports/adapters preserve migration to a separate API or Supabase later.
rejected_alternatives: CAND-003 is infeasible while MCL-1 is unresolved.
CAND-001 remains the strongest fallback if independent/static deployment becomes a hard constraint.
consequences: No Minecraft loader, Supabase SDK, auth provider, queue or cache in the foundation.

risks.statement: MCL-1 may later select a topology that changes the web application's role.
risks.mitigation: Keep domain/application framework-free and re-open ADR-0001 on MCL-1 resolution.

risks.statement: Dependency/toolchain build is not locally verified because npm registry access failed in the generator environment.
risks.mitigation: Require a networked npm install, committed lockfile and full CI before merge.

assumptions.statement: A Node-capable web deployment is acceptable for the first web MVP.
assumptions.review_trigger: Hosting or product-format decision establishes a static-only/independent backend constraint.

review_triggers: hosting rules exclude a Node/Next runtime
offline conflict resolution becomes a core requirement
migration_signals: Extract API when independent ownership/release or materially different scaling is demonstrated.
Add a Minecraft module only after the product-format/loader ADR is approved.
